insight.title: A Shrimp Punches Hotter Than The Sun
insight.subtitle: This tiny crustacean weaponizes a bubble of extreme heat and sound to hunt.

sections.text: The pistol shrimp, no bigger than your thumb, can snap its specialized claw to create a cavitation bubble so powerful, its internal temperature briefly reaches over 4,500 °C.
This incredible feat, known as sonoluminescence, generates a shockwave hot enough to stun prey and even melt small particles of metal. It’s essentially an underwater sonic boom.
Think about it: a creature you could easily overlook generates temperatures comparable to the sun's surface just by closing its claw. Your backyard BBQ seems utterly quaint.
The ocean's smallest brawlers pack a solar punch.
